title: Oh Hyeon-gyu scores early equalizer as South Korea draws 1-1 with Saudi Arabia
text:
Oh Hyeon-gyu scores early equalizer as South Korea draws 1-1 with Saudi Arabia - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 14일(토) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Oh Hyeon-gyu scores early equalizer as South Korea draws 1-1 with Saudi Arabia 
 입력 2026.11.14. 01:00 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Oh Hyeon-gyu (25, Beşiktaş) came through as the decisive player once again. He struck a refreshing equalizer right at the start of the second half.
 The South Korea national soccer team, led by interim coach Robert Moreno, faced Saudi Arabia in an November international friendly at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, Qatar, on Nov. 13 at 11:30 p.m. Korea time. In the FIFA rankings, Korea is 32nd, 23 places higher than Saudi Arabia (55th).
 Korean soccer has not lost to Saudi Arabia in 21 years. Since a 0-1 loss to Saudi Arabia in the August 2005 Asian final qualifying round for the 2006 World Cup in Germany, Korea has gone seven matches without defeat. Korea continued its dominance in the matchup with four wins and three draws.
 Korea also prevailed in their most recent meeting, the 2023 AFC Asian Cup round of 16. Korea fell behind after conceding an early goal to Saudi Arabia but survived when Cho Kyu-seong scored a dramatic equalizer in stoppage time of the second half. Korea then won the penalty shootout 4-2 to advance to the quarterfinals in dramatic fashion.
 Korea aimed to extend its unbeaten run against Saudi Arabia. Moreno started with a 4-4-2 formation again. The starting lineup included Son Heung-min, Oh Hyeon-gyu, Hwang Hee-chan, Hwang In-beom, Park Jin-seop, Cho Hyun-taek, Kim Min-jae, Lee Han-beom, Seol Young-woo and Kim Seung-gyu. All the players from the '96 line who had been at the center of the retirement commotion and rumors of internal strife were named to the squad.
 Korea pushed its line high from the start and controlled the match, but failed to create any clear chances. The team still looked out of sync. In fact, in the fifth minute a high-headed clearance by Kim Min-jae that went forward left Korea exposed to a counterattack.
 The first threatening shot came in the 20th minute. Hwang Hee-chan dropped deep to receive the ball and drove through the central area. He then threaded a through ball into space behind the defense, and the receiving Son Heung-min shot between defenders' legs, but the shot went just wide of the post.
 Saudi Arabia countered. In the 28th minute, Hwang Hee-chan went down in the defensive area after being fouled. Saudi, who recovered the ball, tested Korea's goal with a sharp shot from Al-Sahafi, but Kim Seung-gyu dived to make the save.
 Korea's high pressing rarely worked. The team lacked overall activity and mistimed actions, making them ineffective. Saudi's counterattacks targeting Korea's space behind the defense looked more threatening. In the 42nd minute, Kanno's shot was fortunately saved by Kim Seung-gyu.
 Korea left the first half frustrated. In the 45th minute, Lee Kang-in unleashed a nearly unspinnable, cannon-like shot with his right foot, but the goalkeeper saved it. Immediately after, Hwang In-beom's long-range shot flew off target.
 Just before halftime, Saudi Arabia scored the opening goal. In the first minute of stoppage time, Korea's defense failed to hold the offside line properly, and Al-Sahafi beat Kim Min-jae to go one-on-one with the goalkeeper. To make matters worse, Kim Seung-gyu slipped as he rushed out and conceded the goal.
 But the national team equalized right at the start of the second half. In the second minute, Hwang In-beom won the ball through a high press and Seol Young-woo delivered a low cross from the right. Oh Hyeon-gyu met it with a perfect one-touch finish to rip the net. The goal was Oh Hyeon-gyu's ninth in A internationals, leveling the score at 1-1.
